definitions.explanation: A room in a university or educational institution designed for lectures. Typically has tiered seating arranged for listening to a speaker.

examples.japanese: {講義室|こうぎしつ}に{向|む}かう。
examples.english: To head to the lecture room.

examples.japanese: この{講義室|こうぎしつ}は{三百人|さんびゃくにん}{収容|しゅうよう}できる。
examples.english: This lecture hall can accommodate three hundred people.

examples.japanese: {講義室|こうぎしつ}の{前|まえ}の{席|せき}に{座|すわ}った{方|ほう}が、{先生|せんせい}の{話|はなし}がよく{聞|き}こえる。
examples.english: If you sit in the front of the lecture room, you can hear the professor better.

notes:
A compound of {講義|こうぎ} (lecture) + {室|しつ} (room). Primarily used in university settings for rooms designed for lectures, typically with tiered seating.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {大|だい}{講義室|こうぎしつ}: large lecture hall
- {講義室|こうぎしつ}の{変更|へんこう}: room change for a lecture
- {講義室|こうぎしつ}に{入|はい}る: to enter the lecture room

CONTRAST WITH SIMILAR ROOMS:
- {教室|きょうしつ}: classroom (general, any level — schools and universities)
- {講義室|こうぎしつ}: lecture room (university-specific, larger, for lectures)
- {講堂|こうどう}: auditorium (even larger, for events and ceremonies)
- {演習室|えんしゅうしつ}: seminar room (smaller, for discussion-based classes)

THE ～{室|しつ} SUFFIX:
Common in room names: {会議室|かいぎしつ} (meeting room), {研究室|けんきゅうしつ} (research lab/office), {待合室|まちあいしつ} (waiting room).
